sections.theory:
Kinds of association

There are three kinds of associations which ossibly occur between attributes namely (i) positive association, (ii) negative association and (iii) no association.

(i) In positive association, the presence of one attribute is accompanied by the presence of other attribute(s). For example education and intelligence, health and hygiene are positively associated. In case of positive association, the observed frequency of the combined positive attributes is greater than the expected frequencies i.e.

$(AB)>\frac{(A)(B)}{n}.$

Similar relations hold for other attributes.

(ii) When the presence of an attributes say, A ensures the absence of another attribute say, B or vice-versa, the attributes A and B are said to be negatively associated. For instance, the vaccination and occurrence of disease for which the vaccine is meant for, are negatively associated. In this situation the actual frequency of the cell for combination of attributes is smaller than the expected frequency i.e.

$(AB)<\frac{(A)(B)}{n}.$

(iii) If the two attributes are such that the presence or absence of one attribute has nothing to do with the presence or absence of the other, they are said to be independent. For instance, skin colour and intelligence of persons are independent attributes. If the two attributes A and B are independent, then (AB)=\frac{(A)(B)}{n}. This is known as criterion of independence.

8.1.4 Methods of measures of association

There are mainly three methods of measures of association.

(i) Yule’s coefficient of association.

(ii) Chi-square test for testing hypothesis about independence of attributes in contingency tables.

(iii) Coefficient of contingency for (r × c) contingency table.

Yule’s coefficient of association

Yule’s coefficient of association is named after its inventor G. Undy Yule. It is a relative measure for the strength of association between two attributes say, A and B. It is defined by the formula given below.

$Q=\frac{(AB)(\alpha\beta)-(A\beta)(\alpha B)}{(AB)(\alpha\beta)+(A\beta)(\alpha B)},\qquad -1<Q<+1$

The result of Q is interpreted as:

(ii) کله چې د یوه صفت، لکه A، شتون د بل صفت، لکه B، نشتوالی ډاډمن کړي یا برعکس، نو صفتونه A او B منفي تړاو لري. د بېلګې په توګه واکسین کول او د هغې ناروغۍ پېښېدل چې واکسین ورته جوړ شوی، منفي تړاو لري. په دې حالت کې د صفتونو د ترکیب د خونې اصلي تکرار له تمه شوي تکرار کم وي یعنې

$(AB)<\frac{(A)(B)}{n}.$

(iii) که دوه صفتونه داسې وي چې د یوه صفت شتون یا نشتوالی د بل له شتون یا نشتوالي سره هېڅ اړه ونه لري، خپلواک بلل کېږي. د بېلګې په توګه د خلکو د پوستکي رنګ او هوښیارتیا خپلواک صفتونه دي. که دوه صفتونه A او B خپلواک وي، نو (AB)=\frac{(A)(B)}{n}. دې ته د خپلواکۍ معیار وایي.

8.1.4 د تړاو د اندازه کولو طریقې

د تړاو د اندازه کولو اساساً درې طریقې دي.

(i) د یول د تړاو ضریب.

(ii) په احتمالي جدولونو کې د صفتونو د خپلواکۍ په اړه د فرضیې د ازموینې لپاره د کای مربع ازموینه.

(iii) د (r × c) احتمالي جدول لپاره د احتمالیت ضریب.

د یول د تړاو ضریب

د یول د تړاو ضریب د خپل ایجادګر G. Undy Yule په نوم نومول شوی. دا د دوو صفتونو، لکه A او B، ترمنځ د تړاو د ځواک نسبي اندازه ده. د لاندې فورمول په واسطه تعریف کېږي.

sections.content:
Kinds of association

There are three kinds of associations which ossibly occur between attributes namely (i) positive association, (ii) negative association and (iii) no association.

(i) In positive association, the presence of one attribute is accompanied by the presence of other attribute(s). For example education and intelligence, health and hygiene are positively associated. In case of positive association, the observed frequency of the combined positive attributes is greater than the expected frequencies i.e.

$(AB)>\frac{(A)(B)}{n}.$

Similar relations hold for other attributes.

(ii) When the presence of an attributes say, A ensures the absence of another attribute say, B or vice-versa, the attributes A and B are said to be negatively associated. For instance, the vaccination and occurrence of disease for which the vaccine is meant for, are negatively associated. In this situation the actual frequency of the cell for combination of attributes is smaller than the expected frequency i.e.

$(AB)<\frac{(A)(B)}{n}.$

(iii) If the two attributes are such that the presence or absence of one attribute has nothing to do with the presence or absence of the other, they are said to be independent. For instance, skin colour and intelligence of persons are independent attributes. If the two attributes A and B are independent, then (AB)=\frac{(A)(B)}{n}. This is known as criterion of independence.

8.1.4 Methods of measures of association

There are mainly three methods of measures of association.

(i) Yule’s coefficient of association.

(ii) Chi-square test for testing hypothesis about independence of attributes in contingency tables.

(iii) Coefficient of contingency for (r × c) contingency table.

Yule’s coefficient of association

Yule’s coefficient of association is named after its inventor G. Undy Yule. It is a relative measure for the strength of association between two attributes say, A and B. It is defined by the formula given below.

$Q=\frac{(AB)(\alpha\beta)-(A\beta)(\alpha B)}{(AB)(\alpha\beta)+(A\beta)(\alpha B)},\qquad -1<Q<+1$

The result of Q is interpreted as:
